question: Why is hydrochlorothiazide short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 3 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 2 presentations, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 1 plant links on 1 labels; 1 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.title: What FDA says about this shortage
steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug, and any listing that names one of our own package NDCs.
steps.finding: Not on FDA's current shortage list.

steps.title: Who else makes it
steps.purpose: List every labeler of this drug in the same form, and the plants their labels name.
steps.finding: 37 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 6 inspections (1 OAI at our plants), 0 compliance actions, 0 import-alert listings, 0 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 1 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

steps.title: What we decided last time
steps.purpose: Recall past decisions on this drug from H-MEM, with who approved them.

explanation.headline: Not on FDA's shortage list; FDA's record shows actions at plants on our labels

sentences.text: FDA's drug shortage list does not include hydrochlorothiazide as of 2026-10-21.
Corvale East holds 231 tablets of the 25 mg presentation at 11.6 tablets per day, giving 19.9 days on hand.
Corvale General holds 262 tablets of the 25 mg presentation at 13.8 tablets per day, giving 19 days on hand.
The label for NDC 51655027226 names Northwind Health Company, LLC as the labeler and plant (FEI 1831143) with a VAI inspection on 2025-09-26.
That plant, Northwind Pharmaceuticals LLC, received an OAI classification on 2015-12-09 and VAI classifications on 2015-09-14, 2018-11-16, and 2025-09-26.
The rule's top option is to buy from Accord Healthcare Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and whose label names no plant we could place.
Secondary options are Actavis Pharma, Inc. and Aurobindo Pharma Limited, also not on the shortage list and with no placeable plant on their labels.

rejected.text: Hydrochlorothiazide is not on FDA's shortage list; Corvale sites have 19-20 days on hand and the rule recommends buying from Accord Healthcare Inc.
rejected.reason: headline: 20 is not the days on hand figure in the cited rows

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on carboplatin: restrict carboplatin to curative-intent regimens while on allocation; oncology reviews each palliative order. Rationale: Two suppliers on allocation and under 10 days on hand at Corvale General (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.
